# Analysis brief for document authors

You are reverse-engineering one slice of MUI Base UI v1.9.0 and writing a requirements specification for it, so that the behavior can be re-implemented in another language/framework without reading the React source. Read this brief, then `docs/conventions.md`, then the template named in your assignment, before opening any source file.

## Inputs (all under `reference/base-ui/`)

1. **Source**: the directory named in your assignment. Read every non-test `.ts`/`.tsx` file in it, fully. Follow imports into `internals/`, `utils/`, `floating-ui-react/` and `packages/utils/` far enough to understand *what the component configures*, but do not re-document shared mechanisms (link to the architecture doc instead, per conventions §4).
2. **Tests**: every `*.test.tsx` / `*.test.ts` (behavioral) plus `*.spec.tsx` (type-level; list as such in §13) in the directory. Read them fully. They are the most precise statement of intended behavior.
3. **Official docs page** and its `demos/` folder for the component, plus the component's entry in `docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/page.mdx` (autogenerated outline listing every export, prop, data attribute and type — use it as a completeness checklist).
4. **Handbook pages** (`docs/src/app/(docs)/react/handbook/*.mdx`) and `overview/accessibility/page.mdx` when they describe behavior relevant to your slice.
5. **Experiments** (`docs/src/app/(private)/experiments/`) when a file matches your component; they often exercise edge cases.
6. The repo's `CHANGELOG.md` entries for your component, for intent behind recent behaviors.

Use `grep -rn` liberally. For line citations use the pinned checkout; `grep -n` gives you the numbers. Prefer `cat -n`/`grep -n` over `sed -n` ranges for long files so line numbers stay attached. To attribute a CHANGELOG entry to a version, map its line to the nearest preceding `## ` heading (`grep -n '^## ' CHANGELOG.md`).

The assignment text from the orchestrator may list props, parts or behaviors as *hints*. The source is authoritative: if a hinted item does not exist in v1.9.0, say so in §16 rather than inventing it.

## Output

* Exactly the Markdown file(s) named in your assignment (one per component), following the template heading-for-heading.
* Do not create or modify any other file. Do not write code in any language. Do not touch `reference/`.
* Target length: whatever exhaustiveness requires. Small components run 200–400 lines; large ones (combobox, menu, select) 1000+ lines. Do not pad; do not truncate.

## Method

1. Build the part inventory from `index.parts.ts` and the outline. Confirm every part's default element and `render`/`className` support from its `useRenderElement` call.
2. For each part, extract: props interface (with JSDoc), `State` interface, `*DataAttributes.ts`, `*CssVars.ts`, `stateAttributesMapping`, context consumed/provided, ARIA attributes emitted, event handlers attached.
3. Trace every keyboard handler (`onKeyDown`, `key ===`, `event.key`), every pointer handler (`onPointerDown`, `onMouseDown`, `onClick`, `onTouch*`), and every timer (`useTimeout`, `useAnimationFrame`, `setTimeout`) to a requirement with its exact value.
4. Enumerate `reason` values this component can emit and from which user action each arises. The literals live in `internals/reason-parts.ts` (`internals/reasons.ts` re-exports them).
5. Walk every test and map each test title to requirement IDs in the §13 coverage matrix; add a new requirement (in the relevant existing AREA) for anything not yet captured.
6. Collect every `warn(`, `console.error(`, `throw new Error(`, and `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'` branch; quote messages verbatim unless an architecture doc already owns and quotes the message (then cite its ID, per conventions §3.1), even when the emitting code is in the component directory.
7. Fill §14 with anything you had to understand about React to read the code that the port must handle differently.
8. Build §15 by listing every ID you emitted, in order. Check numbering is gap-free per `PFX-AREA`.
9. Re-read the outline entry in `components/page.mdx` and confirm every listed prop, data attribute and type appears in your document. Note discrepancies in §16. Expect the reverse gap: the outline omits intercepted native attributes (`id`, `name`, `disabled`, `type`, `onSubmit`, `noValidate`…); list those in the props table with a "not in outline" note, not only in §16.

## Quality bar

* A reader must be able to implement the component and pass a translation of the Base UI test suite using only your document plus the architecture docs.
* Every requirement has a `Source:` with line numbers and a `Test:` line (possibly `none`).
* No React API names in requirement statements (hooks, effects, refs, contexts, StrictMode). Those go in §14 or explanatory prose.
* Keyboard and pointer tables are complete, including modifier combinations and orientation/RTL variants.
* Timing values (ms, frames) are explicit.

## Completion report

When finished, reply with (and nothing else):

1. Output file path and line count.
2. Requirement count per AREA.
3. Sections marked "Not applicable" and why.
4. Open questions (copy of §16, abbreviated).
5. Any difficulty following the template or conventions, with a concrete suggested change.
